desc:
Two people want to schedule a meeting inside a day that spans the time range [0, dayLength), counted in whole minutes. Each person's busy time is a list of half-open intervals [start, end), sorted by start, where each meeting ends no later than the next one starts (endi ≤ starti+1), and every interval lies inside the day.

A meeting of duration minutes that starts at minute t occupies [t, t + duration). It is possible if it fits in the day (t + duration ≤ dayLength) and does not overlap any busy interval of either person. Two half-open intervals overlap when each starts before the other ends, so a meeting may begin exactly when a busy interval ends.

Return the earliest possible start minute t, or -1 if no slot exists.

busyA = [[0, 5], [8, 12]]
busyB = [[3, 9], [14, 16]]
duration = 2, dayLength = 20
result = 12

Together they are busy during minutes 0 to 12, and both are free during minutes 12 and 13, so the first start with two free minutes for both is 12. With duration = 3 the gap [12, 14) is too short and the answer would be 16.
constraints: 0 ≤ start < end ≤ dayLength for every interval
hints: Trying every start minute is impossible when the day has 10<sup>9</sup> minutes. Only the end times of busy intervals matter as candidate start times.
Keep a candidate start t, initially 0, and a pointer into each schedule. If a busy interval overlaps [t, t + duration), the candidate must jump to the end of that interval.

Skip intervals with end ≤ t in each list. If the front interval of a list has start < t + duration it blocks the candidate: set t to its end and re-check both lists. If neither blocks, answer t. If t + duration > dayLength, answer -1.
editorial: Think of the answer as a candidate start t that only ever moves right. Begin with t = 0. In each schedule, intervals ending at or before t are in the past and are skipped permanently. The front interval that remains either starts at or after t + duration, in which case it does not interfere (and neither does anything after it), or it starts earlier and it overlaps the window. In the overlapping case no start before its end can work, so move t to that end.

Repeat until neither schedule blocks the window (return t) or until the window no longer fits inside the day (return -1). Each jump retires one busy interval for good, so the loop runs at most n + m + 1 times: O(n + m) time and O(1) extra space. This is the two-pointer view of merging the two schedules and scanning for the first gap that is long enough.
